issues.description: A version cap is asserted without a stated postcondition or termination criterion
issues.detail: The patch pins setuptools<82 in three places and labels the constraint with FIXME and a link to an upstream issue. There is no precondition stating which versions of mmcv/mmengine require pkg_resources, no postcondition stating when the cap may be lifted, and no termination function (e.g., the upstream tag or version that resolves issue #3325). A FIXME without a falsifiable condition for removal is a smuggled goto into the future of the build system; it will not be reasoned about, only forgotten.

issues.description: Runtime dependency in core/setup.py reasoned about as a CI fix
issues.detail: The CI scripts may legitimately constrain setuptools to make the build go through, but core/setup.py declares an install_requires-adjacent constraint that propagates to every downstream user of autogluon.core, not just CI. The precondition `setuptools<82` is required only when constructing mmcv from source; the postcondition of installing autogluon.core does not require it at runtime. The frame has been widened beyond what the bug demands. State precisely why end-users must downgrade their setuptools, or move the constraint to the CI layer where it belongs.

issues.description: Switch from mim to pip with --no-build-isolation lacks a stated invariant
issues.detail: Previously mmcv was installed via mim, which selected a prebuilt wheel matching the torch/cuda environment. The new line `pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` forces a source build in the ambient environment and relies on whatever compiler, torch, and CUDA happen to be present. The author should state the loop invariant of the CI environment (which torch, which CUDA, which compiler) under which this command is known to terminate successfully, and what happens when any of those drift. Without it, this is TESTED-NOT-PROVED: it worked once in CI and will silently break.

issues.description: Ordering of pip install commands is load-bearing but undocumented
issues.detail: The script now installs setuptools<82, then mmcv with --no-build-isolation, then mmengine, then mmdet. The correctness of this sequence depends on mmcv being built before mmengine and mmdet declare conflicting setuptools requirements, and on pip's resolver not upgrading setuptools mid-sequence. A one-line comment stating the invariant `setuptools<82 must hold throughout the four installs` would make the reasoning explicit instead of folklore.

issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 without a stated rationale
issues.detail: Two changes are bundled: switching mmengine to a PyPI wheel, and bumping mmdet to 3.3.0. The latter is unjustified in the diff. Either it is required by mmengine 0.10.7 (state it) or it is gratuitous scope (drop it). Bundling unexplained version changes into a fix labelled `CI: Fix mmengine failure` is the kind of compromise that erodes the ability to reason about future failures.

The body contains no statement of the problem, the reasoning, or the chosen resolution. The reader is forced to reverse-engineer the fix from the diff and an external issue link. State the precondition (setuptools 82 removed pkg_resources, breaking mmcv build), the postcondition (CI green with mmcv 2.1.0, mmengine 0.10.7, mmdet 3.3.0), and the termination condition for the FIXME.

review.summary: This is a TESTED-NOT-PROVED patch: an upstream incompatibility (setuptools>=82 removed pkg_resources, breaking mmcv's build) is worked around by capping setuptools in three locations and switching from mim-managed wheels to a source build under --no-build-isolation. The mechanics will likely make CI green today, but the patch declares no invariant under which the constraint holds, no termination function for the FIXME, and no precondition justifying that core/setup.py — a runtime package metadata file — must propagate a build-time CI constraint to every downstream user. The mmdet bump from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 is bundled in without justification. REFUSED until (a) the setuptools<82 constraint in core/setup.py is either justified as a runtime requirement or moved to the CI layer, (b) the FIXME states the precise upstream condition under which it will be removed, and (c) the mmdet version bump is either justified or dropped. The CI fix itself is plausible; the reasoning around it is absent.
